beats.trigger: ## From Personal to Team
beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: You can't really share an agent.
beats.got: There are four things you can hand over instead of 'the agent', and I'm meant to choose between them.

beats.trigger: Bring one example from your own organisation where people got access to a tool and did not use it.
beats.got: I have this example already: the licences nobody opened. It's the first thing in the day that is about my own company.

beats.trigger: Find the absorption bottleneck and draft the technical plan and the people plan together
beats.got: nothing new. It's a list of verbs and none of them has a cost, a risk or a payback attached.

beats.trigger: What would you want a teammate to have: your `memory/` folder, one of your skills, the morning output, or a way to ask the agent a question in Slack?
beats.got: The question assumes I already run an agent with a memory folder and skills. I don't, so I can't answer it.

beats.trigger: Your agent, skill, output or interface is a candidate for hire: does it do the job better than what they currently use?
beats.got: The Jobs-to-be-Done frame is a fair way to compare options. It's the first thing in the module I could use on a spreadsheet.

beats.trigger: If it could describe anyone in the room, point to the generic line and ask the agent to try that part again.
beats.got: I paste a prompt, Claude reads a lot of files, and I check the output for generic lines. It doesn't say what any of this costs or how long it takes.

beats.trigger: If the reason is *"we already have the platform,"* send it back.
beats.got: Choosing a tool because it fits the infrastructure is the mistake I have watched three programmes make, and this line says so.

beats.trigger: finds what would stop that candidate from being absorbed
beats.got: nothing new. It's a link to the next exercise.

beats.trigger: Find the obstacle that decides whether the teammate can absorb it, then draft both halves of the plan.
beats.got: Now I'm asked to write two plans. I'd want to know first what the thing costs.

beats.trigger: A good bottleneck explains why several other obstacles stay hard.
beats.got: One root cause that keeps several problems hard is a useful test. It's the same thing I ask in a budget review.

beats.trigger: A polished technical file beside a people file full of unnamed roles is the finding, not a finished rollout.
beats.got: Unnamed owners are the reason my programmes failed, and the module says it before I have to raise it. That earns some credit.

beats.trigger: imagines the failure
beats.got: nothing new. It's another link.

beats.trigger: The technical and people plans are hypotheses.
beats.got: The plan is called a hypothesis, which is honest. I'd rather see that than a promise.

beats.trigger: what would have to be true for this teammate, doing this job, to fire their current hire and use my candidate?
beats.got: Roger Martin's question is a good one. I'd use it on a vendor pitch.

beats.trigger: one person, one question about how they do the job today, and one selected assumption with its test.
beats.got: The outcome is one named person, one question and one test. That is small and checkable, and I could do it next week.

beats.trigger: A candidate picked because it fits the infrastructure is shopping.
beats.got: Choosing by outcome is design, and choosing by what we already own is shopping. I can use that sentence in the leadership team.

beats.trigger: ## Lecture: Access is not absorption
beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: The two get reported as one number and they are not one thing.
beats.got: The licence count we report to the board is a count of switches flipped, not of work changed. This is the best point of the day for me.

beats.trigger: The leadership had not done the analysis.
beats.got: A good proposal went nowhere because leaders had not done the work themselves. I've seen that. The 'who knows about the future' line at the end is the sort of thing I tune out.

beats.trigger: The fourth does not copy at all, which is why the product being sold as a shared agent is always three of the four parts, with the fourth still sitting with whoever built it.
beats.got: The accountability is what you can't buy. A vendor's 'shared agent' leaves the answerable person with whoever built it. I should ask who that is before any purchase.

beats.trigger: Share an interface, and someone has to keep it running and answer for it when it is wrong.
beats.got: Each option has a running cost in somebody's time. Nobody says how much time.

beats.trigger: Your candidate is not competing with nothing. It is competing with that.
beats.got: The thing I'd replace is a spreadsheet and a controller's judgement, and that is what any AI tool has to beat.

beats.trigger: Have the conversation before you build anything more.
beats.got: Talk to one person before spending money. That is the cheapest next step on offer.

beats.trigger: Who gets your context, who gets a skill, who wants only the output, and who would use an @mention?
beats.got: nothing new. It's a sorting game with four labels, and I have no agent to share.

beats.trigger: Access is a switch someone flips. Absorption happens in other people's weeks.
beats.got: A summary of what I already read, and it sticks.

beats.trigger: Their answer is the evidence. The plan is still the hypothesis.
beats.got: I'm asked to bring evidence and not a plan. That's the right standard.

beats.trigger: ## Next
beats.got: nothing new

take_homes: Licences sold and licences used are two different numbers. I should ask for the usage figure before I sign off on any rollout.
Before buying anything, ask who answers for it when it is wrong. That person can't be copied or purchased.
Start from the job the person does today and what it currently costs them, and compare the tool against that.

monday.move: Ask my controller how the month-end variance commentary gets written today, who does it and how long it takes. Then decide whether an agent test is worth setting up.
monday.stop_condition: If the commentary takes under about two hours a month, or if IT won't clear the tool for finance data, I drop it.
monday.blocker: IT has not approved the tool for finance data. I also still don't have a per-user monthly cost.

misconception.why: The line about access and absorption being reported as one number describes our licence reporting. I still believe a good part of this is a purchase decision, because the module never gave a cost or a payback.

one_line: Two or three good lines on why licences don't equal use, but no number anywhere, and the exercises assume you already run an agent.
